mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that lowers the risk-free rate, reducing the discount rate for equity valuations and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 4.0% indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes a slowdown in consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 4.0%, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals a broad-based contraction in consumer demand, which typically triggers a sell-off in equity markets, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the interaction Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a supply-driven expansion (INDPRO growth above 0.5% monthly), manufacturing activity is robust, supporting corporate profits and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO growth exceeds 0.5%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising quarterly GDP growth rate (GDPC1) indicates expanding economic activity, which typically supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 rises, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the year-over-year CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 5.0% signals accelerating inflation, which typically prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 5.0%, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) and an increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a deteriorating labor market, which typically reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises, or the interaction Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), the Federal Reserve's policy rate hikes increase borrowing costs and reduce liquidity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.
